observation.visible_scene: A night-sky fireworks display over a dark horizon. A fixed white street-lamp glows at left and faint ground/orange lights sit along the bottom edge; these stay at constant pixel positions, indicating a static camera. The main content is a cluster of yellow-green sparks in the upper-center and a cluster of red sparks just below-right of it, plus a vertical column of bright falling dots near the center-bottom that becomes prominent partway through.
visible_changes: From frame 1 the green cluster (upper-center) and red cluster (mid-right) are already bright and present; over the excerpt both expand outward into more separated individual sparks and gradually lose brightness rather than translating as a whole.

A vertical line of bright white/green dots appears below the clusters around frames 6-7 and persists to the end, with its dots progressing downward, consistent with falling embers (or their reflection).

The red cluster's bright core drifts slightly right and downward through the middle frames, then in the late frames (31-41) a new brighter white/green core is visible near center with the red core to its left, while the original dispersed green sparks fade.
Individual spark points spread radially from the two main cores, increasing the apparent size of the burst over time (expansion, not camera motion).
outside_clip_unknowns: The initial launch/ignition that produced the on-screen bursts is not shown; the segment begins mid-display.
The final fade-out of the sparks and any subsequent bursts are not shown; the segment ends while sparks are still visible.
Whether the central vertical column is falling embers or a water reflection cannot be determined from these frames.
uncertain_details: The exact cause of the late bright white core (new burst vs. re-ignition of falling sparks) is not supported by the frames.
Camera motion is essentially absent given the fixed lamp and horizon, but minor handheld jitter cannot be fully ruled out.
